launches.name: Redstone MRLV | Mercury-Redstone 2
launches.mission_desc: Mercury-Redstone 2 (MR-2) was the test flight of the Mercury-Redstone Launch Vehicle just prior to the first crewed American space mission in Project Mercury. Carrying a chimpanzee named Ham on a suborbital flight, Mercury spacecraft Number 5 was launched at 16:55 UTC on January 31, 1961 from LC-5 at Cape Canaveral, Florida. The capsule and Ham landed safely in the Atlantic Ocean 16 minutes and 39 seconds after launch.

launches.name: Thor DM-21 Agena-B | KH-5 1
launches.mission_desc: KH-5 (Keyhole 5, codenamed Argon) was the area survey component of the Corona program.

launches.name: Atlas LV-3B | Mercury-Atlas 2
launches.mission_desc: Mercury-Atlas 2 (MA-2) was an unmanned test flight of the Mercury program using the Atlas rocket. It launched on February 21, 1961 at 14:10 UTC, from Launch Complex 14 at Cape Canaveral, Florida.

launches.name: Thor DM-21 Ablestar | Transit 3B & LOFTI-1
launches.fail_reason: Failed to seperate from upper stage, failed to place into correct orbit.

launches.name: Little Joe | LJ-5A
launches.mission_desc: Uncrewed launch escape system test of the Mercury spacecraft, conducted as part of the U.S. Mercury program. It was an attempted re-test of the failed Little Joe 5 flight.

launches.name: Redstone MRLV | Mercury-Redstone BD
launches.mission_desc: Mercury-Redstone BD was an uncrewed booster development flight in the U.S. Mercury program. It was launched on March 24, 1961 from Launch Complex 5 at Cape Canaveral, Florida. The mission used a boilerplate Mercury spacecraft and Redstone MRLV-5.

launches.name: Thor DM-21 Agena-B | Discoverer 22
launches.fail_reason: Second stage failed to achieve orbit.

launches.name: Thor DM-21 Agena-B | KH-5 2
launches.mission_desc: KH-5 (Keyhole 5, codenamed Argon) was the area survey component of the Corona program.

launches.name: Vostok-K | Vostok 1
launches.mission_desc: The first crewed space launch & the first orbital launch. It carried the Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin who completed 1 orbit before safely re-entering the atmosphere, he ejected from his capsule at an altitude of 7 km in order to parachute safely to the ground. The mission lasted 108 minutes.

launches.name: Trailblazer 1 | Trailblazer 1g
launches.mission_desc: An experiment where an actual 'artificial meteorite' was flown. This was a 5.8 g steel pellet, which was driven into the atmosphere at 6 km/sec by a 'seventh stage', a shaped charge that accelerated the pellet after burnout of the rocket's six stage. This experiment provided a known reference by which the size of actual meteoroids could be measured according to the luminance of their trails.

launches.name: Atlas LV-3B | Mercury-Atlas 3
launches.mission_desc: Uncrewed test flight of the Mercury program. The launch proceeded normally until about T+20 seconds when the pitch and roll sequence failed to initiate and the vehicle instead just continued flying straight upward, requiring early termination of the flight.
launches.fail_reason: Pitch and roll sequence failed to initiate.

launches.name: Little Joe | LJ-5B
launches.mission_desc: Little Joe 5B was an uncrewed launch escape system test of the Mercury spacecraft, conducted as part of the US Mercury program.

launches.name: Redstone MRLV | Mercury-Redstone 3
launches.mission_desc: Mercury-Redstone 3, or Freedom 7, was the first United States human spaceflight, on May 5, 1961, piloted by astronaut Alan Shepard. It was the first manned flight of Project Mercury, the objective of which was to put an astronaut into orbit around the Earth and return him safely. Shepard's mission was a 15-minute suborbital flight with the primary objective of demonstrating his ability to withstand the high g-forces of launch and atmospheric re-entry.

launches.name: Juno II | S-45A
launches.fail_reason: Second stage failed to achieve orbit.

launches.name: Thor DM-21 Agena-B | KH-5 3
launches.mission_desc: KH-5 (Keyhole 5, codenamed Argon) was the area survey component of the Corona program.

launches.name: Thor DM-21 Ablestar | Transit 4A & Injun-1 & Solrad 3
Redstone MRLV | Mercury-Redstone 4
launches.mission_desc: Mercury-Redstone 4 was the second United States human spaceflight, on July 21, 1961. The suborbital Project Mercury flight was launched with a Mercury-Redstone Launch Vehicle, MRLV-8. The spacecraft, Mercury capsule #11, was nicknamed the Liberty Bell 7, and it was piloted by the astronaut Virgil "Gus" Grissom.

launches.name: Thor DM-21 Agena-B | KH-5 4
launches.mission_desc: KH-5 (Keyhole 5, codenamed Argon) was the area survey component of the Corona program.

launches.name: Vostok-K | Vostok 2
launches.mission_desc: The second crewed space launch carrying the Soviet cosmonaut Gherman Titov to orbit. The mission lasted 25 hours and 18 minutes and completed 17.5 orbits. He remains the youngest person to reach space, being a month short of 26 at the time of the launch.

launches.name: Blue Scout Jr | O-1
launches.mission_desc: A flight to measure particle densities in the Van Allen belts.

launches.name: Atlas LV-3B | Mercury-Atlas 4
launches.mission_desc: Mercury-Atlas 4 was an uncrewed suborbital test flight of the Mercury program.

launches.name: Scout X-1 | P-21
launches.mission_desc: A flight carrying plasma and aeronomy research payloads on a suborbital trajectory

launches.name: Saturn I | Saturn SA-1
launches.mission_desc: First test flight of the Saturn I launch vehicle and first mission of the Apollo program.

launches.name: Blue Scout II | Mercury-Scout 1
launches.mission_desc: Mercury-Scout 1, or MS-1, was a United States spacecraft intended to test tracking stations for Project Mercury flights. The launch of Mercury-Scout 1 on November 1, 1961 was unsuccessful, and the satellite failed to achieve orbit.

launches.name: Atlas LV-3B | Mercury-Atlas 5
launches.mission_desc: Mercury-Atlas 5 was an American spaceflight of the Mercury program. It was launched on November 29, 1961, with Enos, a chimpanzee, aboard. The craft orbited the Earth twice and splashed down about 200 miles (320 km) south of Bermuda, and Enos became the first primate from the United States and the third great ape to orbit the Earth.

launches.name: Blue Scout Jr | Blue Scout Jr. O-2
launches.mission_desc: A flight carrying particle detectors. It was the only completely successful flight of the initial Blue Scout Junior program.

launches.name: Vostok-K | Zenit-2 1
launches.mission_desc: Zenit-2 film-return and ELINT reconnaissance satellite.
